summary: Lassen NF lookout on Magee Peak, built 1917 after Lassen summit station was shattered; staffed 1917-1932; fate disputed (removed vs burned).

facts.design: Building fourteen feet square with glass sides; observer sat in a wheeled chair
facts.status_note: Kemnow page marks it removed, with no date; SummitPost says it burned long ago; sources disagree

access.note: Reached by forest roads and a trail from the trailhead, per a climbing guide

visit.trail_note: Magee trail no longer maintained by the Forest Service; downed trees on the trail and at the trailhead; road still passable

events.note: Telephone line completed to the summit; lookout planned for the next season
Substitute station built after an early Lassen eruption shattered the forest bureau's lookout on Lassen summit
Contractor J.G. Fritz held the construction contract in July; substitute station completed by late July 1917
W.S. Hays of Montgomery Creek stationed there as lookout
Mrs. Todd Williams of Portland took the lookout position in June 1918; name spelled Tod in a July item
Mrs. Ted Williams back for a second season; called the first woman lookout in the Lassen forest
T.D. Goodman, forest lookout on the summit, telephoned news that Lassen had opened in eruption
T.D. Goodman took up duties for the fire season; moved off in October after snow
Goodman expected back on duty; a 1932 item says he had been there about 17 years

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Newspapers give 8,025 ft, about 10,000 ft, 7,000 ft and 9,000 ft. No single figure is adopted; the story reports the disagreement.
Kemnow page says removed, with no date; SummitPost says it burned long ago. Both are reported; the record stays gone with status_note.

notes_for_editor: Two sources: Kemnow's page (about a dozen newspaper items, 1915-1932) and a SummitPost climbing guide. Status conflict: removed (no date) vs burned long ago; not resolved. Name variants: Magee/McGee; Williams spelled Todd, Tod and Ted; Goodman's 'about 17 years' (1932) does not square with the 1918-1919 Williams items. Web searches turned up no corroboration for Goodman or the Williams names, and a Wikipedia lead says there was once a watchtower but gives no dates (not cited). Next places to check: Lassen National Forest history or archives, the Lassen Historical Society, and the 1918 and 1930s Lassen forest reports. Record agency matches the Kemnow header.
